day_shape: 98 items: US Treasury's 'Operation Economic Outcast' hits Iran rail/auto/metals sectors, UKMTO reports tanker struck in Strait of Hormuz, UK arrests dual UK-Iranian national over RAF Fairford plot, additional US Patriots deployed to Saudi Arabia and Qatar, UK defends snapback at UNGA after Russia/China vetoes.

threads.label: US sanctions blitz on Iran industry
threads.summary: The US State Department and Treasury announced new sanctions under 'Operation Economic Outcast' targeting networks in Iran's rail, automotive and metals sectors across the Middle East, East Asia and Europe. Iran International reported the designations expand Washington's pressure campaign on some of Iran's largest industrial companies.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz tanker and Gulf air defences
threads.summary: UKMTO reported a tanker struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, while reports said the US deployed two additional Patriot batteries in Saudi Arabia and Qatar to protect oil and gas facilities. Defa Press cited Axios saying the deployments followed renewed Trump threats against Iran.

threads.label: UK snapback and Iran-linked UK plots
threads.summary: UK Ambassador Sarah MacIntosh told the UN General Assembly that UN sanctions on Iranian proliferation remain in force despite Russian and Chinese vetoes of the Panel of Experts mandate. British counter-terrorism police arrested a UK-Iranian dual national over a thwarted attack on RAF Fairford, with Iran International linking Tehran to both that case and the Flydubai incident.

threads.label: Nuclear diplomacy signalling
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in private talks Iran would restore inspector access to bombed nuclear sites in exchange for sanctions relief, while a senior defence official said Tehran was weighing responses to US pressure. Trump told Time he was considering ramping up bombing of Iran after the US midterms and separately claimed he eliminated Iran's nuclear threat in a single night.

threads.label: IDF Gaza disclosures on hostages and media
threads.summary: The IDF said Izz al-Din al-Bik, commander of Hamas's Northern Gaza Brigade killed earlier this week, had commanded the captivity of Israeli hostages and participated in the October 7 infiltration. The IDF also released a list identifying 170 Palestinians presented as journalists killed in Gaza as members of Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad and other groups.

threads.label: Yemen front and Saudi interceptions
threads.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Khamis Mushait and four drones, while a Yemeni air force spokesperson reported 20 strikes on Houthi targets in Taiz province. IRIB claimed the Saudi-appointed Presidential Council of Yemen announced the killing of special forces commander Brigadier Muhammad al-Khoulani in Taiz.

threads.label: Iran internal security and executions
threads.summary: Iran International reported four men detained during January's nationwide protests were sentenced to death by Tehran Revolutionary Courts. The Jerusalem Post said IRGC killed six people described as 'terrorists' in Zahedan after reportedly seizing explosives, while IRIB reported armed clashes with a terrorist group in Rask county, Sistan and Baluchestan.
